draft.title: Returning cultural objects
card: Cultural objects are things made or used by a people, such as carvings, tools, statues and sacred items. Ancestral remains are the bodies of people who lived long ago.
Many objects and ancestral remains were taken from the places and communities they came from. This often happened in colonial times, when one country ruled another.
Many were taken to museums and private collections far away, often in other countries. The communities they came from had little say in this.
Today some of these objects and remains are being returned to their communities. This is called repatriation. It can help a community look after its own heritage and honour its ancestors.
draft.remember: Many objects and remains were taken during colonial times. Some are now returned to their communities.

a.q: What is repatriation of cultural objects?
opts: Returning objects or remains to the community they came from
Moving objects between museums so more people see them
Buying objects from a community so they can be displayed
Making copies of objects so the originals can be kept safe
a.why: Repatriation means sending objects or ancestral remains back to the communities they were taken from. Moving them between museums is different, because they stay away from their home communities.
a.clue: Think about where the objects end up.

b.q: A carved wooden shield was taken from a village by a colonial officer in the 1880s. It has been in a museum overseas ever since. Why might the village ask for it back?
opts: It was taken from their community and is part of their past
The museum has not looked after it and cannot display it
The shield is too old for anyone to be allowed to study
Colonial rule ended, so museums must now return all objects
b.why: The shield was taken from the village, and it is part of the community's heritage, so the village may want it returned. The last option is tempting, but the card says only that some objects are being returned, not that all must be.
b.clue: Think about who the shield belongs to in the story.

a.best: Returning objects or remains to the community they came from

b.best: It was taken from their community and is part of their past
